entities.summary: Franz Wenzel, Graf von Kaunitz-Rietberg was an Austrian general who led the Austrian forces during the Seven Years' War (1756-1763) and played a key role in the Wars of the French Revolution. He was a prominent figure in the Austrian military during this period, known for his bravery and strategic thinking. Wenzel's military career spanned several decades, with notable engagements in Prussia, Bohemia, and the Italian peninsula. His legacy as a military leader has endured, with many historians recognizing his contributions to the development of modern military tactics. Despite his significant impact on European military history, Wenzel's personal life remains somewhat of a mystery, with limited information available on his family, education, and early career. Nevertheless, his reputation as a skilled and courageous commander has been cemented in the annals of Austrian military history.
